sources.entry: sglang - A high-performance serving framework for large language models and multimodal models.

summary.one_liner: SGLang is an open-source inference framework for serving large language, vision-language, and diffusion models, with a focus on agentic workloads, large-scale serving, and RL rollouts.
summary.what_it_does: SGLang serves large language, vision-language, and diffusion models for inference. The README says it is optimized for agentic workloads, large-scale serving, and RL rollouts. It includes SGLang Diffusion, a built-in engine for image and video generation, shipped in the same repository and Python package. Installation is offered as a Docker image (lmsysorg/sglang:latest) or a Python package installed with uv. Hardware support is listed across NVIDIA, AMD, Google TPU, Intel GPU/CPU, Apple Silicon (Metal/MLX), Huawei Ascend NPUs, and Moore Threads GPUs. The README also describes an ecosystem of related projects for audio serving, speculative decoding (SpecForge), RL training integrations, and deployment/orchestration. Model launching is guided by a Quickstart and a Cookbook, which the README points to rather than detailing inline.
use_cases: serve an open LLM behind an API for production traffic
run vision-language models on GPUs or TPUs
generate images or video with diffusion models
supply rollout generation for RL post-training
run LLM inference on Apple Silicon or Ascend NPUs
how_to_run: Follow the Quickstart in the docs to launch a model and send a request
Use the Cookbook to pick a model and hardware for a ready-to-run launch command
git clone the repo and run: pip install -e "python" (for development)
notable: Covers LLMs, vision-language, and diffusion models (image and video) in one framework
Broad hardware support including NVIDIA, AMD, Google TPU, Intel, Apple Silicon, Huawei Ascend, and Moore Threads
Built-in SGLang Diffusion engine for image and video generation
Part of a larger ecosystem with RL trainers (verl, slime, Miles, AReaL, Tunix) and orchestration options (Ray Serve, NVIDIA Dynamo)
Acknowledges reuse of design and code from Guidance, vLLM, LightLLM, FlashInfer, Outlines, and LMQL
caveats: Several hardware platforms (AWS Trainium, Cambricon MLU, MetaX, and others) are listed only as integrations in progress
The README points to the Cookbook and platform guides for model compatibility and setup rather than listing supported models inline
Enterprise adoption, consulting, and sponsorship are handled by contacting the maintainers; no pricing is stated
